title: Economics Test 1 (Indian Economy Basics — most probable)

questions.q: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country means:
options: The total income earned by government in a year
The total value of exports only
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within the country in a year
The money printed by the central bank in a year
questions.explain: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) counts only final goods and services produced inside the country's borders, by Indians and foreigners alike.

questions.q: Gross National Product (GNP) is calculated as:
options: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) plus net income earned from abroad
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) plus government borrowings
Only the income of farmers and factories
questions.explain: Gross National Product (GNP) adds what Indians earn abroad (minus what foreigners earn in India) to Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

questions.q: Per capita income of a country is obtained by dividing:
options: National income by the number of workers
Government income by the number of states
National income by the total population
questions.explain: Per capita income is simply the average income per person — total national income divided by population.

questions.q: In India, the official estimates of national income are prepared by the:
options: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)
questions.explain: The National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics, compiles national income and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.

questions.q: Agriculture, animal husbandry, fishing and mining belong to which sector of the economy?
questions.explain: The primary sector takes things directly from nature; manufacturing is secondary and services form the tertiary sector.

questions.q: Manufacturing and industries, which convert raw materials into finished goods, belong to the:
questions.explain: The secondary sector processes primary products — for example, cotton (primary) into cloth (secondary).

questions.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
questions.explain: Services like trade, transport, banking and information technology contribute more than half of India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), though agriculture employs the most people.

questions.q: Which sector employs the largest number of people in India?
questions.explain: Even though its share in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has fallen, agriculture still gives work to the largest share of India's population.

questions.q: Inflation in an economy means:
options: A fall in prices of all goods
Rise in price of one item for one day
Increase in the supply of goods
A general and continuous rise in prices
questions.explain: When inflation rises, the purchasing power of money falls — the same money buys less than before.

questions.q: Retail inflation in India, which affects the common person's cost of living, is measured mainly by the:
questions.explain: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks prices of goods and services households buy; the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sets its inflation target in Consumer Price Index (CPI) terms.

questions.q: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures changes in prices at the:
questions.explain: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) covers goods traded in bulk and does not include services, unlike the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

questions.q: Fiscal policy of a country — relating to taxation and government spending — is framed by the:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
questions.explain: Fiscal policy is the government's tool (taxes and expenditure), while monetary policy belongs to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

questions.q: Monetary policy of India — controlling money supply and interest rates — is framed by the:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explain: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), through its Monetary Policy Committee, decides the repo rate and other money controls.

questions.q: Repo rate is the rate at which:
options: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) borrows from banks
The public deposits money in banks
Commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
The government borrows from the public
questions.explain: When the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raises the repo rate, loans become costlier, which helps control inflation.

questions.q: Reverse repo rate is the rate at which:
options: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) borrows money from commercial banks
Banks borrow from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
questions.explain: Reverse repo is the opposite of repo — banks park their extra funds with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and earn this rate.

questions.q: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of a bank's deposits that it must keep as cash with the:
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explain: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is fixed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI); raising it reduces the money banks can lend.

questions.q: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requires banks to maintain a part of their deposits in:
options: Liquid assets like cash, gold and government securities
questions.explain: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), like Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), is a reserve requirement decided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

questions.q: Bank rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends money to banks for the:
questions.explain: Bank rate is the long-term lending rate of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), while repo serves shorter-term needs.

questions.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mean:
options: Buying and selling of government securities to control money supply
questions.explain: Through Open Market Operations (OMO), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sells securities to absorb extra money and buys them to inject money.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established in the year:
questions.explain: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) began working on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was nationalised in the year:
questions.explain: Established in 1935 as a shareholders' bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was nationalised on 1 January 1949 — the two years are asked as a pair.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is located at:
questions.explain: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) first worked from Kolkata but shifted its headquarters to Mumbai in 1937.

questions.q: Currency notes in India (except the one-rupee note) are issued by the:
questions.explain: Notes of two rupees and above bear the signature of the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

questions.q: The one-rupee note in India is issued by the:
options: Ministry of Finance (signed by the Finance Secretary)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explain: The one-rupee note and all coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance — the single exception to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rule.

questions.q: India's First Five Year Plan (1951-56) gave the highest priority to:
questions.explain: The First Five Year Plan focused on food production and irrigation after Partition; heavy industry came with the Second Plan.

questions.q: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), based on the model of Professor P.C. Mahalanobis, emphasised:
questions.explain: Steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were set up under the Mahalanobis strategy of the Second Plan.

questions.q: The Green Revolution in India is associated with a big increase in the production of:
questions.explain: New high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation raised foodgrain output sharply from the late 1960s.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the father of the Green Revolution in India?
questions.explain: Dr M.S. Swaminathan led the scientific side of India's Green Revolution; Norman Borlaug was its global pioneer.

questions.q: The White Revolution in India is related to increased production of:
questions.explain: Operation Flood made India the world's largest milk producer — this was the White Revolution.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of the White Revolution in India?
questions.explain: Dr Verghese Kurien built the Amul cooperative model at Anand, Gujarat, which powered the White Revolution.

questions.q: The Planning Commission of India, which prepared the Five Year Plans, was set up in the year:
questions.explain: The Planning Commission was created in March 1950 and worked till it was replaced in 2015.

questions.q: According to the Census of India 2011, the literacy rate of India was about:
questions.explain: Census 2011 recorded literacy at 74.04% — male literacy about 82% and female literacy about 65%.

questions.q: According to the Census of India 2011, the sex ratio of India (females per 1,000 males) was:
questions.explain: The 2011 sex ratio was 943; Kerala had the highest sex ratio among states, above 1,000.

questions.q: According to the Census of India 2011, the population density of India was about:
questions.explain: Density rose from 325 in 2001 to 382 in 2011; Bihar was the most densely populated state.

questions.q: The total population of India as per the Census of 2011 was about:
questions.explain: Census 2011 counted about 121 crore people, making India then the second most populous country.

questions.q: Disguised unemployment — where more people work than are actually needed — is most commonly found in Indian:
questions.explain: In disguised unemployment, removing some workers from a family farm would not reduce its output at all.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published every year by the:
questions.explain: The Human Development Index (HDI) ranks countries by health, education and income; it is released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

questions.q: The Indian economy is best described as a:
questions.explain: India has both private enterprise and a public sector — this combination is called a mixed economy.

questions.q: The growth of an economy is best measured by a sustained rise in its:
questions.explain: Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) removes the effect of price rise, so it shows the true increase in production.

questions.q: The foreign exchange reserves of India are held and managed by the:
questions.explain: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) keeps India's foreign currency assets and gold reserves safe.
